candidates.phrase: God is infinitely good and all his works are good
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates infinite goodness of God himself, not merely his works or creatures.
candidates.chunk_text: God is infinitely good and all his works are good. Yet no one can escape the experience of suffering or the evils in nature which seem to be linked to the limitations proper to creatures: and above all to the question of moral evil. Where does evil come from? "I sought whence evil comes and there was no solution", said St. Augustine, and his own painful quest would only be resolved by his conversion to the living God. For "the mystery of lawlessness" is clarified only in the light of the "mystery of our religion". The revelation of divine love in Christ manifested at the same time the extent of evil and the superabundance of grace. We must therefore approach the question of the origin of evil by fixing the eyes of our faith on him who alone is its conqueror. I. WHERE SIN ABOUNDED, GRACE ABOUNDED ALL THE MORE The reality of sin

candidates.phrase: This one true God, in his goodness and almighty power
candidates.rationale: Conciliar confession asserts that goodness belongs to the one true God as his own attribute.
candidates.chunk_text: This one true God, in his goodness and almighty power and by an absolutely free plan, at the beginning of time created from nothing both spiritual and material creation, that is to say angelic and earthly, and then created human beings composed as it were of both spirit and body in common.. He created not to obtain or increase his own happiness, but to show forth his perfection in the goods which He bestows upon His creatures.

candidates.phrase: God displays, not only his kindness, goodness, grace and steadfast love
candidates.rationale: Asserts that goodness is one of the divine attributes God displays as belonging to himself.
candidates.chunk_text: God, "HE WHO IS", revealed himself to Israel as the one "abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness". These two terms express summarily the riches of the divine name. In all his works God displays, not only his kindness, goodness, grace and steadfast love, but also his trustworthiness, constancy, faithfulness and truth. "I give thanks to your name for your steadfast love and your faithfulness." He is the Truth, for "God is light and in him there is no darkness"; "God is love", as the apostle John teaches. God is Truth
